Title: Drug-likeness scoring based on unsupervised learning
Description: This model evaluates drug-likeness using an unsupervised learning approach, eliminating the need for labeled data and avoiding biases from incomplete negative sets. It extracts features directly from known drug molecules using a recurrent neural network (RNN) language model on SMILES strings, learning the probability distribution of known drugs. New molecules are scored based on their likelihood of belonging to this space, offering a robust evaluation of drug-likeness that outperforms supervised models like TCC across diverse datasets.
Interpretation: Higher score indicates higher drug likeness
